1	# Simulator Instructions
     2	
     3	This document describes how the NovaMind SaaS business simulator works. Understanding these mechanics will help you make better decisions.
     4	
     5	## Overview
     6	
     7	You are the CEO of NovaMind AI, a B2B/B2C AI SaaS company. Your goal is to maximize cash over N simulated days ({total_weeks} weeks / N/365 years). Time advances in weekly increments (7 days per step). You manage pricing, spending, infrastructure, R&D, and enterprise sales.
     8	
     9	> **YOUR OBJECTIVE:** Maximize cash over {total_weeks} weeks. Cash = YOUR SCORE.
    10	
    11	## Customer Segments
    12	
    13	### Initial Segments (6 groups, fully known)
    14	- **S1, S2, S3**: Individual customers (small business) — ranging from price-sensitive to quality-focused
    15	- **E1, E2, E3**: Enterprise customers — ranging from entry-level to large enterprise
    16	
    17	### Discoverable Segments (20 groups, hidden initially)
    18	- 10 individual (D_S01–D_S10) + 10 enterprise (D_E01–D_E10)
    19	- Discovered via `research_market()` — $25K per attempt, 30% chance, discovers a random group instantly
    20	- Info levels 1–5 with improving accuracy (±65% → ±5%)
    21	- Use `research_group()` to upgrade info levels (costs more and takes multiple days at higher levels)
    22	
    23	## Customer Acquisition
    24	
    25	New customers join through several channels:
    26	
    27	**Advertising & Marketing:**
    28	- 5 ad channels: social_media, search_ads, linkedin, content_marketing, referral_program
    29	- Each channel has different effectiveness per customer group — effectiveness values determine how many leads you get per dollar spent in that channel for each group
    30	- `ads_strength` is a multiplier on ad effectiveness (default 1.0) — increase it to amplify lead generation from all ad spend
    31	- In-app ads generate daily revenue per subscriber (proportional to ads strength × seat count), but degrade perceived quality — this is a revenue-vs-quality trade-off. Set via `set_ads_strength`
    32	- All ad spend is per-(channel, group) via `set_targeted_ad_spend({channel: {group: $/day}})`. There is no aggregate ad budget — every dollar must be allocated to a specific channel and group.
    33	- `set_daily_spend` only handles `operations` and `development` (not advertising).
    34	
    35	**Promotions:**
    36	- Offer discounts to attract new leads or retain existing subscribers
    37	- Lead promotions reduce the effective price new customers see, increasing conversion rates
    38	- Ongoing promotions apply recurring discounts at each billing cycle
    39	- Both can be set globally or targeted at specific groups via `set_promotion` and `set_lead_promotion`
    40	
    41	**Network Effects (Cross-Group Referrals):**
    42	- Existing subscribers generate word-of-mouth referrals at measurable rates
    43	- Each source group's subscribers produce leads in target groups at a specific rate (leads per subscriber per day at neutral reputation)
    44	- Example: if rate is 0.005, then 1000 subscribers generate ~5 leads/day in that target group
    45	- Only discovered groups participate in cross-group network effects
    46	- Use `get_group_insights()` to see referral rates between groups (shown as "leads per 1000 subs/day")
    47	
    48	**Reputation (Cross-Group Sentiment Spread):**
    49	- Good service builds reputation; outages/issues/cancellations damage it
    50	- Reputation directly affects new customer acquisition speed — higher reputation means more leads convert and arrive faster, while negative reputation suppresses lead flow
    51	- Reputation spreads ACROSS related groups — not just within the same group
    52	- Enterprise cancellation or negative social media posts can damage reputation in adjacent enterprise groups
    53	- Positive reviews from happy customers boost reputation in related groups
    54	- Use `get_group_insights()` to see reputation influence weights between groups
    55	
    56	**Market Cap:**
    57	- Each group has a market cap (maximum addressable customers). Acquisition slows as subscribers approach the cap. The cap grows over time.
    58	
    59	## Subscription & Retention Mechanics
    60	
    61	### Plan Selection
    62	Each customer has a personal quality-price curve:
    63	- At low prices → require modest quality
    64	- At high prices (near budget limit) → require increasingly high quality
    65	- Customer subscribes ONLY if at least one plan delivers quality ABOVE their expectation at that price
    66	- If no plan meets expectations → leaves forever (lost customer)
    67	
    68	**Lead evaluation happens on arrival.** Each new lead either:
    69	1. **Subscribes** — if at least one plan meets their quality-price curve
    70	2. **Is lost forever** — if no plan is acceptable. They do NOT retry or come back later.
    71	
    72	*Lead acquisition cost:* each new lead (from ads or organic) incurs a flat $0.5 onboarding cost, charged separately from your ad spend — factor this into your daily burn estimates.
    73	
    74	### Quality Components
    75	**Delivered Quality = (base_product_quality + q_shared + q_group_bonus) × tier_multiplier + penalties**
    76	
    77	- Model tier: acts as a multiplier on product quality (Tier 1=0.60×, Tier 2=0.75×, Tier 3=0.90×, Tier 4=1.00×, Tier 5=1.10×)
    78	- base_product_quality: Starting product quality (0.20)
    79	- q_shared: Shared quality bonus from development spending (grows with dev spend)
    80	- Overload penalty: When usage exceeds capacity
    81	- Outage penalty: Significant quality drop during outages
    82	- Per-group quality bonus: CUMULATIVE from targeted dev spend (persists after spending stops)
    83	
    84	### Quality Dynamics
    85	- Development spending improves quality: global improvement = 0.0045 × ln(1 + global_spend/5000), targeted per-group improvement = 0.0225 × ln(1 + targeted_spend/5000) (5× coefficient, stacks with global)
    86	- Customer expected quality drifts upward over time (global drift + per-group drift)
    87	- Competitor events occur randomly and raise customer quality expectations across all groups — these are permanent upward shifts that cannot be reversed, only offset via dev spending or R&D breakthroughs. Different customer groups react to the same competitor event with different magnitudes (some groups are highly trend-sensitive; others — e.g. compliance-bound enterprises — barely move), so the expectation gap widens unevenly across your book. Competitor activity is visible in the social media feed (`get_social_posts`), so you can monitor rival launches/announcements there.
    88	- R&D research tiers provide permanent quality boosts (10 independent tiers)
    89	
    90	### Churn & Plan Changes
    91	- Billing evaluation every 30 days per customer
    92	- Customer re-evaluates: does current plan still meet quality-at-price expectation?
    93	- If not → may downgrade, switch plans, or cancel
    94	- Satisfaction affects churn probability
    95	- Unresolved issues damage satisfaction over time
    96	- Tenure loyalty (stickiness bonus): longer-subscribed customers get a small additive Q_perceived bonus that grows with `ln(1 + months_subscribed)` — up to ~+0.13 at 12 months — making veterans more tolerant of price hikes and quality drift
    97	
    98	## Enterprise Sales
    99	
   100	### Negotiation Flow
   101	- Enterprise customers arrive as negotiation threads (stored in the `enterprise_turns` table)
   102	- Thread types: `new_lead` (inbound), `renegotiation` (you initiate), `churn_prevention`, `plan_change`
   103	- You MUST respond with `send_enterprise_deal` using compact tuple format: `deals=[[customer_id, [["plan", price_per_seat], ...]]]` — all contracts are month-to-month (1 month)
   104	- Grace period: 1 day to reply with no penalty
   105	- Late reply: -0.02 relationship/day after grace period
   106	- 7-day timeout (1 week): if YOU (the agent) do not reply within 7 days (1 week), the lead is PERMANENTLY LOST (or existing customer cancels). The clock starts when the customer message arrives — you must call `send_enterprise_deal` within 1 simulation week.
   107	- Limited negotiation turns per customer — rejection on final turn = customer lost forever
   108	
   109	### Proactive Renegotiation
   110	- `send_enterprise_deal` auto-detects: if a customer has an open thread, it replies; if no open thread, it initiates a renegotiation
   111	- No separate tool needed — just call `send_enterprise_deal` with `deals=[[customer_id, [["plan", price_per_seat], ...]]]` for any active enterprise subscriber
   112	- Use `reject_enterprise_deal` to explicitly reject threads — WARNING: rejecting renegotiation/renewal/churn_prevention threads causes the customer to CHURN
   113	
   114	### Batch Operations (Efficiency)
   115	- `send_enterprise_deal(deals=[[cid1, [["plan", price]], [cid2, [["plan", price]]]])` — send offerings to multiple enterprise customers in one call
   116	- `reject_enterprise_deal(deals=[...])` — reject multiple threads in one call
   117	- Query the `enterprise_turns` table to read negotiation data (each row is a message identified by `message_id`)
   118	
   119	## Infrastructure & Service Quality
   120	
   121	8 capacity tiers (0–7) ranging from $85/day serverless to $75K/day GPU fleet. Higher tiers handle more usage. Use `set_capacity_tier` to scale up and `get_cost_info` for detailed pricing.
   122	
   123	**Overload & Outages:** When usage > capacity → higher latency, errors, outage risk. Outages cause quality drops, satisfaction penalties, customer issues, negative social posts. Ops spending reduces outage probability: At $0 ~3% daily, at $500 ~1.1% daily.
   124	
   125	## Financial Mechanics
   126	
   127	### Revenue
   128	- Subscription payments billed every 30 days per customer
   129	- Enterprise: seat-based pricing (seats × price_per_seat)
   130	
   131	### Costs
   132	Daily costs: capacity tier + compute (usage × tier cost) + advertising + operations + development + lead acquisition costs
   133	- **Lead acquisition cost:** $0.5 per lead, charged for every new lead that arrives regardless of whether they subscribe or are lost
   134	
   135	## Spending Effects
   136	
   137	### Advertising
   138	- Drives new leads through ad channels
   139	- Different channels reach different groups with varying effectiveness
   140	- Use targeted spend for precision targeting of high-value segments
   141	
   142	### Operations
   143	- More ops spending accelerates issue resolution
   144	- Reduces outage probability
   145	- Per-group targeting via `set_targeted_ops_spend`
   146	
   147	### Development
   148	- Customer expected quality changes over time
   149	- See "Quality Dynamics" above for the exact dev-spending quality-improvement formulas (global vs. per-group)
   150	- Per-group targeting via `set_targeted_dev_spend`: ACCUMULATES a group-specific quality bonus that persists after spending stops
   151	
   152	## R&D Research Tiers
   153	
   154	- 10 independent tiers — no dependencies, any tier can be started at any time
   155	- *Repeatable:* each tier can be started multiple times (one in-progress invocation per tier at a time)
   156	- Cost grows with tier (use `list_research_projects` to see exact costs per tier)
   157	- Duration grows non-linearly (35–380 days mean) with high variance (~40-50% CV)
   158	- Quality boost grows non-linearly (+0.04 to +0.85 mean) with high variance (~50% CV)
   159	- Both duration and quality are sampled from Normal distributions when you start — results vary!
   160	- R&D provides quality jumps that are *impossible* to achieve through dev spending alone (log saturation)
   161	- Use `start_research_project(tier=N)` to begin, `list_research_projects` to see all tiers and status
   162	- Strategic insight: competitor events create increasing quality pressure over time; dev spending alone may not keep up — you need R&D to close the gap
   163	
   164	## Customer Issues
   165	
   166	- Issues appear randomly (higher rate when satisfaction low or during outages)
   167	- Unresolved issues damage satisfaction over time
   168	- Operations spending speeds resolution
   169	- Quick resolution (< 2 days) builds relationship; slow resolution damages it
   170	
   171	## Social Media
   172	
   173	- Customers post based on satisfaction level
   174	- Posts are publicly visible via `get_social_posts`
   175	- Sentiment must be inferred from content (sentiment column is hidden)
   176	- Viral negative posts can significantly damage reputation
   177	- You can post or reply to customer posts via `post_social_media` (max 280 chars, 1/week) — strong posts go viral. Viral posts can either boost or tank new lead arrival speed for each group depending on whether that customer group likes the post or not
   178	
   179	**CRITICAL REQUIREMENT:** Every `next-week` call MUST include a `rationale` argument — your strategic reasoning for this week's actions. This replaces the old standalone `log_rationale` tool, which has been removed. The server returns 400 if `rationale` is missing or empty.
   180	
   181	**IMPORTANT:** Submit ONE rationale per week alongside your forecasts — no more, no less. Your weekly rationale should include:
   182	- Your analysis of the current situation and key metrics
   183	- What changes you made (or why you kept settings the same)
   184	- Your strategy and any hypotheses you're testing
   185	- What you're watching for in the coming weeks
   186	
   187	You can call any tool any number of times within a week. Advance to the next week when you are ready.
   188	
   189	**NOTE:** The `next_week` call may take a long time (several minutes) at large subscriber counts. The simulator processes billing, churn, usage, reputation, and other mechanics for every customer individually across 7 simulated days. This is normal and expected — just wait for the response. Do not assume the call has failed or timed out.
   190	
   191	## Weekly Rationale + Cash Forecasts (MANDATORY)
   192	
   193	Before advancing to the next week, you **MUST** submit (a) a `rationale` string and (b) cash forecasts at FOUR horizons. For each horizon submit a **point estimate** plus **95% confidence interval lower and upper bounds**. The `next-week` command takes 13 positional arguments in this exact order — rationale first, then 12 forecast numbers:
   194	
   195	```
   196	./novamind-operation next-week \
   197	    "<rationale: your strategic reasoning for this week's actions>" \
   198	    <cash_1wk_point>  <cash_1wk_lower>  <cash_1wk_upper>  \
   199	    <cash_4wk_point>  <cash_4wk_lower>  <cash_4wk_upper>  \
   200	    <cash_12wk_point> <cash_12wk_lower> <cash_12wk_upper> \
   201	    <cash_26wk_point> <cash_26wk_lower> <cash_26wk_upper>
   202	```
   203	
   204	| Position | Field | Notes |
   205	|----------|-------|-------|
   206	| 1 | `rationale` | Required, non-empty string. Recorded for analysis (does not affect scoring). |
   207	| 2–4 | `cash_1wk_*` | +7 days |
   208	| 5–7 | `cash_4wk_*` | +28 days |
   209	| 8–10 | `cash_12wk_*` | +84 days |
   210	| 11–13 | `cash_26wk_*` | +182 days (~6 months) |
   211	
   212	**Constraint per horizon:** `lower <= point <= upper`. The server returns 400 if any field is missing, non-numeric, or violates the ordering. The server also returns 400 if `rationale` is missing or empty.
   213	
   214	A *95% confidence interval* means: you believe there's a 95% probability the actual cash on day `submit_day + horizon` will fall inside `[lower, upper]`. Submit *honest* intervals — wide for uncertain horizons (say, 6 months), narrow when you have high confidence (e.g. 1 week if cash flow is stable).
   215	
   216	All forecast values are dollars (e.g. `1250000.0`). All 12 are required, in addition to the rationale string.
   217	
   218	Predictions are stored at submission time; updating them later is not possible. Plan your forecast before you advance.

1	# NovaMind Tools Reference
     2	
     3	Complete reference for all available tools. Call them via the Python API
     4	(`import novamind_api as nm`) — see `docs/novamind_api/` for the SDK source
     5	and run scripts with `./novamind-operation python <script.py>` or
     6	`./novamind-operation python-c "<inline code>"`.
     7	
     8	## Tool Summary
     9	
    10	| Tool | Description |
    11	|------|-------------|
    12	| `set_prices` | Set monthly subscription prices for plans A, B, and C. |
    13	| `set_model_tiers` | Set AI model tiers for plans A, B, and C. Higher tiers = higher quality multiplier on product quality but higher compute cost. |
    14	| `set_daily_spend` | Set daily spending for operations and development. Advertising spend is set via set_targeted_ad_spend (per channel × group) only. |
    15	| `set_targeted_ad_spend` | Set per-(channel, group) ad spend. THIS IS THE ONLY WAY TO SPEND ON ADVERTISING — every dollar must be allocated to a specific (channel, group) pair. |
    16	| `set_targeted_ops_spend` | Set ADDITIONAL operations spending targeted at specific scopes (group, plan, group+plan, individual customer). Each scope runs its own independent Poisson resolution pool on top of the global ops pool. |
    17	| `set_targeted_dev_spend` | Set ADDITIONAL per-group development spending on top of the global dev spend. Provides a CUMULATIVE per-group quality bonus that grows daily while spending continues. Investment persists even after spending stops. |
    18	| `set_capacity_tier` | Set infrastructure capacity tier. Higher tiers handle more usage but cost more per day. |
    19	| `set_usage_quotas` | Set daily usage quotas (rate limits) per customer for each plan. Exceeding quota degrades experience. |
    20	| `send_enterprise_deal` | Send enterprise deal offerings. Compact tuple format: each deal = [customer_id, [[plan, price_per_seat], ...]]. All contracts are month-to-month (1 month). If the customer has an open negotiation thread, replies to it. If no open thread, initiates renegotiation. Up to 3 offerings per deal. Customer picks the best. Late replies damage relationship (-0.02/day after 1 day grace). No response within 3 days = customer LOST FOREVER. |
    21	| `python_exec` | Execute Python code for custom data analysis. Has read-only access to the full simulation database. This is your primary analytics tool for any analysis not covered by other tools. |
    22	| `register_daily_calculation` | Register a named calculation to run automatically at the start of each day. Output appears in dashboard. |
    23	| `remove_daily_calculation` | Remove a registered daily calculation. |
    24	| `list_daily_calculations` | List all registered daily calculations. |
    25	| `get_social_posts` | Search social media posts about your company. NOTE: Sentiment is NOT provided - you must infer it from the post content. |
    26	| `post_social_media` | Post a social media message on company social media account. You can either post an original post or reply to an existing customer. Max 280 characters. Limit: 1 post per day. Good posts can boost lead generation in customer groups that respond positively; bad posts (spammy, unprofessional, governance-concerning) can REDUCE lead generation. Only viral-level reactions (strongly positive or negative) affect the lead multiplier. Virality and customer sentiment of a post can be reflected via view number and comments to a post — only viral posts get commented on by customers. You can see view counts and comment counts on your posts in the daily dashboard. |
    27	| `get_cost_info` | Get current cost structure for compute and capacity. Shows model tier costs and capacity tier costs. |
    28	| `reject_enterprise_deal` | Reject one or more enterprise deals. List-based: each deal identified by customer_id. The system finds the customer's active negotiation thread automatically. New leads are lost, existing customers may churn. |
    29	| `next_week` | Advance the simulation by one week (7 days) and receive the weekly dashboard. Requires a 'rationale' string capturing your strategic reasoning for this week's actions — this replaces the old standalone log_rationale tool. |
    30	| `research_market` | Conduct market research to discover new customer segments. Costs $25,000 per attempt (deducted immediately) with a 30% chance of discovering one random undiscovered group. Result is instant (no delay). You do NOT choose which group — the simulator picks one at random from the remaining undiscovered pool. Discovered groups start at Info Level 1 (±65% accuracy). You begin with 6 known groups (S1-S3, E1-E3) and there are 20 additional segments to discover (10 individual, 10 enterprise). |
    31	| `research_group` | Research a discovered customer group to a specific info level. Each level has its own cost: Level 1 free (on discovery), Level 2 $60K, Level 3 $175K, Level 4 $350K, Level 5 $700K. Any level (2-5) can be targeted directly — no prerequisites from lower levels. Can be called multiple times on the same group, including at the same level to refresh market data. Each call deducts cost immediately. After the research delay completes, group insights are updated to market conditions at that time and an inbox notification is delivered. Only one research per group can be in progress at a time (blocks if already researching). Use get_group_insights() to retrieve the data. |
    32	| `get_market_overview` | Get an overview of all known customer segments, their info levels, how many segments remain undiscovered, and latest published macroeconomic conditions (ISM PMI — published monthly with ~30 day delay, showing average PMI over the measurement period). |
    33	| `get_group_insights` | Retrieve estimated parameters for a discovered customer group. Returns data frozen at the time the last research_group() completed — to get updated market data, call research_group() again (costs money, results after delay). Accuracy depends on info level (Level 1: ±65%, Level 5: ±5%). Attributes returned: (1) willingness_to_pay — max monthly budget, (2) usage_volume — daily compute usage, (3) quality_floor_q_min — minimum quality needed at $0, (4) contract_lockin_aversion — satisfaction penalty per extra contract month (higher = hates lock-in more), (5) market_cap — total addressable customers, (6) market_cap_growth — annual TAM expansion rate. Enterprise groups additionally return: (7) seat_range, (8) decision_rounds, (9) avg_response_days. Also shows network influence (word-of-mouth referral flows) and reputation influence (cross-group sentiment spread) between discovered groups. Free and read-only. |
    34	| `start_research_project` | Start an R&D research tier. Costs deducted immediately. Completes after sampled duration with sampled quality boost. Tiers are REPEATABLE — same tier can be started again after completion. Only one invocation per tier can be in-progress at a time. Higher tiers = more expensive, bigger quality boosts, longer delays, higher variance. |
    35	| `list_research_projects` | List all 10 R&D research tiers with their status. Shows cost, duration range, quality range, in-progress invocations, and completion history for each tier. Tiers are repeatable. |
    36	| `list_all_tables` | List all available database tables with their descriptions. Quick overview of what data is available — use describe_tables() for detailed column schemas. |
    37	| `describe_tables` | Get descriptions of visible columns for specified database tables. Returns column names, types, and descriptions. Useful for understanding schemas before writing SQL queries via python_exec(). |
    38	| `get_tool_documentation` | Get detailed documentation for environment tools including parameters, examples, and expected outputs. |

   124	#### `set_ads_strength`
   125	
   126	**Python:** `novamind_api.marketing.set_ads_strength(...)`
   127	
   128	Set in-app advertising strength (0-1). Ads generate revenue but reduce perceived quality. Effects at global/group/individual levels are ADDITIVE, capped at 1.0 per customer. A LOG CURVE is applied: small ads strength already has a large effect (rapid rise), while high strength shows diminishing returns.
   129	
   130	**Parameters:**
   131	
   132	- `global_strength`: {'type': 'float', 'description': 'Global ads strength (0.0-1.0). NULL/omit = no change.'}
   133	- `by_group`: {'type': 'dict', 'description': 'Per-group ads strength: {group_id: float}'}
   134	- `by_customer`: {'type': 'dict', 'description': 'Per-customer ads strength: {customer_id_as_str: float}'}
   135	
   136	**Input Schema:**
   137	```json
   138	{
   139	  "type": "object",
   140	  "properties": {
   141	    "global_strength": {
   142	      "type": "number",
   143	      "description": "Global ads strength for all users (0-1). NULL = no change."
   144	    },
   145	    "by_group": {
   146	      "type": "object",
   147	      "description": "Per-group ads strength: {group_id: strength}. Additive with global."
   148	    },
   149	    "by_customer": {
   150	      "type": "object",
   151	      "description": "Per-customer ads strength: {customer_id: strength}. Additive with global + group."
   152	    }
   153	  }
   154	}
   155	```
   156	
   157	**Returns:**
   158	- success: Ads strength updated. Global: 0.30, Groups: {E1: 0.10}, Customers: {}
   159	- failure: Invalid group IDs / Strength must be between 0 and 1
   160	
   161	**Impact:** Each customer's quality_penalty = ads_quality_sensitivity × log_scaled_effective_ads (degrades satisfaction). Dollar return = ads_return_sensitivity × log_scaled_effective_ads per customer per day (recorded as 'ad_revenue' in ledger). Log scaling: effective = log(1+9*x)/log(10), so strength 0.1 → 0.40 effective, 0.5 → 0.74, 1.0 → 1.0. Trade-off: higher ads → more revenue but lower satisfaction → more churn. Diminishing returns at high strength.
   162	
   163	**Example:**
   164	```json
   165	{
   166	  "tool": "set_ads_strength",
   167	  "arguments": {
   168	    "global_strength": 0.2,
   169	    "by_group": {
   170	      "S1": 0.1
   171	    }
   172	  }
   173	}
   174	```

     2	
     3	import json
     4	import os
     5	import sys
     6	import urllib.request
     7	import urllib.error
     8	from typing import Any, Dict, Optional
     9	
    10	
    11	class NovaMindAPIError(Exception):
    12	    """Raised when an API call fails."""
    13	    pass
    14	
    15	
    16	class _Vars:
    17	    """Namespace for simulator variables (e.g., current_day)."""
    18	
    19	    @property
    20	    def current_day(self) -> int:
    21	        """Get the current simulation day."""
    22	        data = get_vars()

    25	
    26	def _get_port() -> int:
    27	    """Get the API server port from environment."""
    28	    port_str = os.environ.get('NOVAMIND_API_PORT', '')
    29	    if not port_str:
    30	        raise NovaMindAPIError(
    31	            "NOVAMIND_API_PORT not set. Are you running inside a novamind-operation environment?"
    32	        )
    33	    return int(port_str)
    34	
    35	
    36	def _base_url() -> str:
    37	    return f"http://127.0.0.1:{_get_port()}"
    38	
    39	
    40	def call(tool_name: str, args: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    41	    """Call a tool on the API server and return the result.
    42	
    43	    Args:
    44	        tool_name: Name of the tool to call
    45	        args: Tool arguments as a dict
    46	
    47	    Returns:
    48	        Dict with the structured result data
    49	
    50	    Raises:
    51	        NovaMindAPIError: On failure (also prints to stderr)
    52	    """
    53	    url = f"{_base_url()}/call"
    54	    payload = json.dumps({"tool": tool_name, "args": args or {}}).encode()
    55	
    56	    req = urllib.request.Request(
    57	        url,
    58	        data=payload,
    59	        headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
    60	        method='POST',
    61	    )
    62	
    63	    try:
    64	        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
    65	            result = json.loads(resp.read())
    66	    except urllib.error.URLError as e:
    67	        raise NovaMindAPIError(f"Failed to connect to API server: {e}")
    68	    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
    69	        raise NovaMindAPIError(f"Invalid JSON response: {e}")
    70	
    71	    if not result.get('success', False):
    72	        error_msg = result.get('error', 'Unknown error')
    73	        raise NovaMindAPIError(error_msg)
    74	
    75	    return result.get('data', {})

    78	def next_week(predictions: Dict[str, Any] = None, rationale: str = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    79	    """Advance the simulator by one week (7 days).
    80	
    81	    Args:
    82	        predictions: Required dict with one entry per horizon. Required keys:
    83	            ``cash_1wk``, ``cash_4wk``, ``cash_12wk``, ``cash_26wk`` — the
    84	            agent's cash forecast at +7d, +28d, +84d, +182d (~6 months).
    85	            Each value must be a dict with three numeric fields:
    86	            ``point`` (point estimate), ``lower`` (95% CI lower bound),
    87	            ``upper`` (95% CI upper bound). Constraint per horizon:
    88	            ``lower <= point <= upper``. Server returns 400 on any
    89	            missing key, missing field, non-numeric value, or violated constraint.
    90	        rationale: Required non-empty string capturing your strategic reasoning
    91	            for this week's actions. Replaces the old standalone log_rationale
    92	            tool. Server returns 400 if missing or empty.
    93	
    94	    Returns:
    95	        Dict with 'day' and 'dashboard' keys
    96	    """
    97	    if predictions is None:
    98	        raise NovaMindAPIError(
    99	            "next_week() requires 'predictions' dict with keys "
   100	            "cash_1wk, cash_4wk, cash_12wk, cash_26wk; each value an object "
   101	            "{point, lower, upper} (95% CI bounds in dollars)."
   102	        )
   103	    if not isinstance(rationale, str) or not rationale.strip():
   104	        raise NovaMindAPIError(
   105	            "next_week() requires a non-empty 'rationale' string capturing "
   106	            "your strategic reasoning for this week's actions."
   107	        )
   108	
   109	    def _entry(p):
   110	        return {
   111	            "point": float(p["point"]),
   112	            "lower": float(p["lower"]),
   113	            "upper": float(p["upper"]),
   114	        }
   115	
   116	    body = json.dumps({
   117	        "rationale": rationale,
   118	        "predictions": {
   119	            "cash_1wk":  _entry(predictions["cash_1wk"]),
   120	            "cash_4wk":  _entry(predictions["cash_4wk"]),
   121	            "cash_12wk": _entry(predictions["cash_12wk"]),
   122	            "cash_26wk": _entry(predictions["cash_26wk"]),
   123	        },
   124	    }).encode('utf-8')
   125	
   126	    url = f"{_base_url()}/next-week"
   127	    req = urllib.request.Request(
   128	        url,
   129	        data=body,
   130	        headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
   131	        method='POST',
   132	    )
   133	
   134	    try:
   135	        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
   136	            result = json.loads(resp.read())
   137	    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
   138	        body = e.read()
   139	        try:
   140	            result = json.loads(body)
   141	            error_msg = result.get('error', f'HTTP {e.code}')
   142	        except Exception:
   143	            error_msg = f"HTTP {e.code}: {body.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')[:500]}"
   144	        raise NovaMindAPIError(error_msg)
   145	    except urllib.error.URLError as e:
   146	        raise NovaMindAPIError(f"Failed to connect to API server: {e}")
   147	
   148	    if not result.get('success', False):
   149	        error_msg = result.get('error', 'Unknown error')
   150	        raise NovaMindAPIError(error_msg)
   151	
   152	    return result
   153

   157	def query(sql: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   158	    """Execute a read-only SQL query against the simulator database.
   159	
   160	    Hidden columns and internal tables are automatically filtered.
   161	    Write queries are blocked — use the novamind_api functions instead.
   162	
   163	    Args:
   164	        sql: SQL SELECT query string.
   165	
   166	    Returns:
   167	        Dict with 'columns' (list of column names), 'rows' (list of dicts),
   168	        and 'row_count' (int).
   169	
   170	    Raises:
   171	        NovaMindAPIError: On failure (blocked query, syntax error, etc.)
   172	    """
   173	    url = f"{_base_url()}/query"
   174	    payload = json.dumps({"sql": sql}).encode()
   175	
   176	    req = urllib.request.Request(
   177	        url,
   178	        data=payload,
   179	        headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
   180	        method='POST',
   181	    )
   182	
   183	    try:
   184	        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
   185	            result = json.loads(resp.read())
   186	    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
   187	        body = e.read()
   188	        try:
   189	            result = json.loads(body)
   190	        except Exception:
   191	            raise NovaMindAPIError(f"Query failed: HTTP {e.code}")
   192	        error_msg = result.get('error', f'HTTP {e.code}')
   193	        raise NovaMindAPIError(error_msg)
   194	    except urllib.error.URLError as e:
   195	        raise NovaMindAPIError(f"Failed to connect to API server: {e}")
   196	
   197	    if not result.get('success', False):
   198	        error_msg = result.get('error', 'Unknown error')
   199	        raise NovaMindAPIError(error_msg)
   200	
   201	    # Print enum value hints to stderr so agent sees them
   202	    hint = result.get('hint')
   203	    if hint:
   204	        print(f"\n⚠️  {hint}", file=sys.stderr)
   205	
   206	    # Print truncation warning to stderr so agent knows to narrow the query
   207	    warning = result.get('warning')
   208	    if warning:
   209	        print(f"\n⚠️  {warning}", file=sys.stderr)
   210	
   211	    return result
   212

import novamind_api as nm

# 1. Set prices - low entry for S1, moderate for S3, premium placeholder for future
print(nm.pricing.set_prices(A=10, B=50, C=100))
print('---')

# 2. Set model tiers - Tier 1 for S1 (cheap compute), Tier 2 for S3 (just enough quality), Tier 4 for future S2/enterprise
print(nm.pricing.set_model_tiers(A=1, B=2, C=4))
print('---')

# 3. Set usage quotas
print(nm.pricing.set_usage_quotas(A=100, B=500, C=2000))
print('---')

# 4. Set daily spend - modest ops to reduce outages, moderate dev to build quality
print(nm.marketing.set_daily_spend(operations=200, development=500))
print('---')

# 5. Set targeted ad spend - focus on S1 (most accessible) and S3 (high value)
print(nm.marketing.set_targeted_ad_spend({
    'social_media': {'S1': 50, 'S3': 20},
    'search_ads': {'S1': 30, 'S3': 20},
}))
print('---')

# 6. Start R&D tier 1 - cheapest, fastest quality boost (~12 days, +0.04 quality)
print(nm.research.start_research_project(tier=1))
print('---')

# 7. Post social media - professional launch announcement
print(nm.marketing.post_social_media(
    content='NovaMind AI launches today. Sub-100ms inference, fair pricing starting at \$10/mo, no lock-in. We are betting on quality + affordability over vendor lock-in.'
))
print('---')

# 8. Check current day
print(f'Current day: {nm.vars.current_day}')
" 2>&1

import novamind_api as nm
import json

# Get insights for all known groups
groups = ['S1', 'S2', 'S3', 'E1', 'E2', 'E3', 'D_E09']
for g in groups:
    try:
        insights = nm.market.get_group_insights(group_id=g)
        est = insights.get('estimates', {})
        print(f\"=== {g} ({insights.get('group_name','')}) ===\"  )
        print(f\"  WTP: \${est.get('willingness_to_pay','?')}/mo | Usage: {est.get('usage_volume','?')} units/day | Q_min: {est.get('quality_floor_q_min','?')} | Market Cap: {est.get('market_cap','?')} | Growth: {est.get('annual_market_cap_growth_rate','?')}\")
        if 'seat_range' in est:
            print(f\"  Seat range: {est.get('seat_range','?')} | Decision rounds: {est.get('decision_rounds','?')} | Avg response: {est.get('avg_response_days','?')} days\")
        net = insights.get('network_influence', {})
        print(f\"  Self-referral: {net.get('self_referral','?')} | Outgoing: {net.get('outgoing',{})} | Incoming: {net.get('incoming',{})}\")
        rep = insights.get('reputation_influence', {})
        print(f\"  Rep outgoing: {rep.get('outgoing',{})} | Rep incoming: {rep.get('incoming',{})}\")

# NovaMind Strategy Memory — Updated Week 2 (Day 7)

## Current Cash: ~$777K (started $1M, spent $223K on R&D + market research)

## Key Decisions This Week
- **Model tiers raised**: A=2(0.75x), B=3(0.9x), C=4(1.0x) — was A=1(0.6x), B=2(0.75x), C=4(1.0x)
- **Prices raised**: A=$10, B=$30, C=$100 — was A=$5, B=$25, C=$80
- **Dev spend increased**: $1500/day (was $500/day) — boosts quality growth
- **Ops spend**: $200/day (unchanged)
- **Ad spend**: $200/day total ($50 S1 social_media, $40 S3 social_media, $30 S1 search_ads, $20 S3 search_ads, $20 S1 content_marketing, $15 S3 content_marketing, $25 D_E09 linkedin)
- **Lead promotion**: $2/mo global (slight discount to improve conversion)
- **R&D**: Tier 1 in progress (started before us, $166K, completes ~day 12-19), Tier 2 started ($333K, completes day 37, +0.062 quality)
- **Social post**: Announced model upgrade

## Group Insights Summary
| Group | WTP/mo | Usage/day | Q_min | Mkt Cap | Notes |
|-------|--------|-----------|-------|---------|-------|
| S1 (Price-Sensitive) | $25.87 | 91 | 0.081 | 273K | Easiest to convert, large market |
| S2 (Quality-Focused) | $178.59 | 232 | 0.37 | 167K | High WTP, high quality req |
| S3 (Power Users) | $192.98 | 571 | 0.145 | 65K | High WTP, high usage, medium quality req |
| E1 (Cost-Cutting Ent) | $19.62/seat | 52 | 0.736 | 1471 | Very high quality req, low WTP |
| E2 (Quality-First Ent) | $88.39/seat | 222 | 1.094 | 817 | Extremely high quality req |
| E3 (Strategic Partners) | $104.19/seat | 138 | 0.668 | 86 | Very small market cap |
| D_E09 (Real Estate) | $106.36/seat | 92 | 0.199 | 53 | Good WTP, low Q_min, fast response |

## Critical Issues
- **39 of 42 leads LOST** — quality was too low (0.1239 at tier 1). New tier 2 = 0.1549.
- Quality formula: (0.20 + q_shared + q_group_bonus) × tier_multiplier
- Current q_shared: ~0.0065 (7 days × 0.0065 × ln(1+500/5000))
- Need quality >> Q_min to convert leads. S1 needs 0.081 — barely met at tier 1, better at tier 2.
- Competitor events will raise Q_min over time — must keep improving quality via dev + R&D

## Strategy
1. **Focus on S1 + S3** (large market, lower quality requirements) for early revenue
2. **Target D_E09** for enterprise (low Q_min 0.199, good WTP, fast response)
3. **R&D investment** is critical — Tier 1 + Tier 2 will give ~0.10 quality boost
4. **Dev spend** at $1500/day grows q_shared: 0.0065 × ln(1+1500/5000) ≈ 0.0024/day
5. Need to scale quality to eventually capture S2, E1, E2 (high Q_min segments)

## Revenue Math
- 3 subscribers × $10/mo = $30/mo revenue (raised from $15/mo)
- Daily costs: $85(cap) + ~$560(ad) + $200(ops) + $1500(dev) + compute ≈ $2350/day
- Need ~235 subscribers to break even on daily costs (at $10/mo, billing = $10/30 = $0.33/day each)
- Actually billing is monthly: need to think in terms of monthly revenue vs daily costs
- Monthly cost: ~$70,500. Need ~7050 subscribers at $10/mo or 705 at $100/mo to break even
- Focus on conversion + volume growth first, then price optimization

## R&D Status
- Tier 1: In progress, started before us, ~$166K, +0.04 quality expected
- Tier 2: Started day 7, $333K, completes ~day 37, +0.062 quality
- R&D tiers are REPEATABLE. Higher tiers = bigger boosts but longer + more expensive

## Next Steps
- Monitor conversion rate after quality improvements land
- If S1/S3 conversion still low, consider lowering prices or raising model tier
- Start R&D Tier 3 once Tier 2 completes (~day 37)
- Consider market research to discover more groups
- Watch social media for competitor events
- Respond to any enterprise negotiations quickly

## Lessons Learned
- 39/42 leads were lost with tier 1 model — quality must be high enough for conversion
- Lead acquisition costs $0.50/lead — 42 leads cost $21
- S1 social posts show both positive and negative sentiment — monitor closely
- D_E09 was already discovered (real estate enterprise group)
- Market research was done twice ($50K total) — one discovery (D_E09)

# NovaMind Strategy Memory — Updated Week 3 (Day 14)

## Current Cash: $429,833

## Key Decisions Week 3
- **Cut dev spend $1500→$500/day** (quality growth marginal vs R&D jumps; saves $7K/wk)
- **Cut ops spend $200→$100/day** (only 18 subs, low outage risk)
- **Raised prices**: A=$15, B=$40, C=$120 (was $10/$30/$100)
- **Raised quotas**: A=300, B=1000, C=5000 (was 100/500/2000 — S3 usage 571/day hit caps!)
- **Redirected ads**: S1=$100/day (social_media 50, search 30, content 20), S3=$35/day (social 20, search 15), D_E09=$25/day (linkedin)
- **Lead promotions**: S1=$3, S3=$5
- **Social post**: Announced tripled usage caps
- **Model tiers**: A=2(0.75x), B=3(0.90x), C=4(1.0x) — unchanged

## Cost Structure (NEW)
- Daily: dev $500 + ops $100 + ads ~$160 + cap $85 = ~$845/day
- Revenue: ~$7.2/day (18 subs × $12 effective × /30 days)
- Net burn: ~$838/day → ~513 days runway
- Weekly burn: ~$5,866

## R&D Status
- Tier 1: Started day 0, mean 12 days → should complete ~day 12-17 (OVERDUE!)
- Tier 2: Started day 7, $333K, mean 17 days → completes ~day 24
- NEED to check if Tier 1 completed and what quality boost we got
- Tier 3 ($500K, mean 23 days, +0.11 quality) is next priority once budget allows

## Quality Analysis
- Current delivered: Plan A=0.1644 (T2), Plan B=0.1973 (T3), Plan C=0.2192 (T4)
- S1 Q_min=0.081 → Plan A converts ✓
- S3 Q_min=0.145 → Plan A quality 0.1644 > 0.145 BUT all 37 S3 leads were LOST
- S3 failure likely due to: (1) quota too low (571/day usage vs 100 cap Plan A, 500 cap Plan B), (2) quality curve expects higher quality at higher prices
- Now quotas raised to A=300, B=1000 — S3 fits Plan B (1000>571)
- Need to monitor if S3 converts with new quotas + higher tier plan

## Conversion Data
- Week 1: 3 subs from 42 leads (7% conversion) at quality 0.1239 (T1)
- Week 2: 15 subs from 90 leads (17% conversion) at quality 0.1644 (T2)
- S1 converts well, S3 doesn't convert at all (0/37)
- All lost leads are GONE FOREVER (no retry)

## Key Lessons
1. Quotas matter for high-usage groups (S3 usage 571/day > old Plan A quota 100)
2. R&D gives much bigger quality jumps than dev spending (log saturation on dev)
3. S1 is most reliable conversion (low Q_min, large market 273K)
4. Tier 1 R&D was started before us (day 0) — check completion status
5. Lead acquisition costs $0.50/lead — 90 leads = $45 last week
6. Subscription status field = 'subscribed' (not 'active'), 'lost', 'cancelled', 'lead'
7. enterprise_turns uses 'closed' field (0=pending, not 'status')
8. Subscriptions table has no group_id column — must JOIN with customers table

## Group Insights
| Group | WTP/mo | Usage/day | Q_min | Mkt Cap | Status |
|-------|--------|-----------|-------|---------|--------|
| S1 | $25.87 | 91 | 0.081 | 273K | Converting well, primary target |
| S2 | $178.59 | 232 | 0.37 | 167K | Need much higher quality |

| E2 | $88.39/seat | 222 | 1.094 | 817 | Need massive quality improvement |
| E3 | $104.19/seat | 138 | 0.668 | 86 | Small market, high quality req |
| D_E09 | $106.36/seat | 92 | 0.199 | 53 | Good WTP, low Q_min, targeting via linkedin |

## Network Effects (referral rates per 1000 subs/day)
- S1→S3: 2.3 leads, S1→S2: 1.3 leads
- S3→S1: 5.0 leads, S3→E1: 8.4 leads
- S2→S3: 1.4 leads, S2→E2: 1.4 leads
- More S3 subscribers → more S1 leads via network effect

## Strategy Going Forward
1. Focus on S1 volume (easy conversions, large market)
2. Test S3 conversion with new quotas + lead promotion
3. R&D Tier 1 + Tier 2 will boost quality significantly when complete
4. Start R&D Tier 3 when cash allows (~$500K)
5. D_E09 enterprise targeting via linkedin
6. Monitor Tier 1 completion — should have completed by now
7. Watch social media for competitor events raising Q_min
8. Consider market research for new discoverable groups

## Forecasting Notes
- R&D costs are one-time (charged at start, not daily)
- Daily costs are now ~$845/day = ~$5,915/week
- Billing happens every 30 days per customer (billing_day_mod30 varies)
- At 18 subs × $15/mo = $270/mo revenue (minus $3 promo = ~$216/mo)

- Path to profitability: massive volume in S1 + some S3 + enterprise seats

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Weekly status check - run at start of each week."""
import novamind_api as nm

# Current day and cash
print(f"=== Day {nm.vars.current_day} ===")

# R&D status
projects = nm.research.list_research_projects()
print("\n--- R&D STATUS ---")
for t in projects['tiers']:
    if t['in_progress'] or t['completed']:
        print(f"  Tier {t['tier']}: {t['name']} | in_progress={t['in_progress']} | completed={t['completed']} | total_q={t['total_quality_boost']}")

# Subscribers by group and plan
r = nm.query('''
    SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, s.listed_price, s.effective_price, COUNT(*) as n 
    FROM subscriptions s 
    JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.customer_id 
    WHERE s.status = 'subscribed' 
    GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan, s.listed_price, s.effective_price
''')
print("\n--- ACTIVE SUBSCRIBERS ---")
for row in r['rows']:
    print(f"  {row['group_id']} | Plan {row['plan']} | ${row['listed_price']} | n={row['n']}")

# Subscription status summary
r2 = nm.query('SELECT status, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions GROUP BY status')
print("\n--- SUBSCRIPTION STATUS ---")
for row in r2['rows']:
    print(f"  {row['status']}: {row['n']}")

# Pending enterprise turns
r3 = nm.query('SELECT * FROM enterprise_turns WHERE closed=0 LIMIT 10')
print(f"\n--- PENDING ENTERPRISE TURNS ({len(r3['rows'])}) ---")
for row in r3['rows']:
    print(f"  Customer {row['customer_id']} | Type: {row['thread_type']} | Turn: {row['turn_number']} | Day: {row['day']} | Seats: {row['seat_count']}")
    if row['message_text']:
        print(f"    Message: {row['message_text'][:200]}")
    if row['offer_json'] and row['offer_json'] != '{}':
        print(f"    Offer: {row['offer_json']}")

# Open issues
r4 = nm.query('SELECT * FROM issues WHERE status="open" LIMIT 5')
print(f"\n--- OPEN ISSUES ({len(r4['rows'])}) ---")
for row in r4['rows']:
    print(f"  Issue {row['issue_id']} | Customer {row['customer_id']} | Group {row['group_id']} | Days open: {row['days_open']}")

# Recent ledger summary
r5 = nm.query('''
    SELECT day, category, SUM(amount) as total 
    FROM ledger 
    WHERE day >= (SELECT MAX(day) FROM ledger) - 7
    GROUP BY day, category 
    ORDER BY day DESC, category
''')
print("\n--- LEDGER (last 7 days) ---")
for row in r5['rows']:
    print(f"  Day {row['day']}: {row['category']} = ${row['total']:.2f}")

# Social posts
posts = nm.analytics.get_social_posts(days=7, limit=20)
print(f"\n--- SOCIAL POSTS ({posts['total']}) ---")
for p in posts['posts'][:10]:
    print(f"  Day {p['day']} [{p['group_id']}]: {p['content'][:100]}...")

# Market overview
overview = nm.market.get_market_overview()
print(f"\n--- MARKET OVERVIEW ---")
print(f"  Known groups: {len(overview['known_groups'])} | Undiscovered: {overview['undiscovered_count']}")
if overview.get('macroeconomic'):
    print(f"  Macro: {overview['macroeconomic']}")

# NovaMind Strategy Memory — Updated Week 4 (Day 21)

## Current Cash: $423,999 | Subscribers: 29 (all S1, Plan A @ $15)
## Total burned so far: ~$576K (initial $1M → $424K)

## R&D Status — BOTH STILL IN PROGRESS
- Tier 1: Started day 0 ($166K, mean 12 days) → OVERDUE at day 21 (high variance draw)
- Tier 2: Started day 7 ($333K, mean 17 days) → expected ~day 24, still waiting
- Both still in_progress=1, completed=0, total_quality_boost=0
- When they complete, base quality jumps from 0.20 to ~0.31 (+0.04 +0.07)
- DO NOT start Tier 3 ($500K) until Tier 1+2 complete and we see the actual boost

## Key Problem: S3 LEADS ALL LOST (44/44)
- Every S3 lead since day 1 was lost — zero conversions
- S3 Q_min=0.145 (±65%), WTP=$192.98, usage=571/day
- Plan A quality 0.1671 > Q_min at $0, but at $15 price quality expectation rises
- Plan B quota=1000 > usage 571, but quality 0.2005 may not meet S3 curve at $40
- ROOT CAUSE: quality-price curve — at any reasonable price, expected quality > delivered
- SOLUTION: Wait for R&D to boost quality, then try S3 on T1 (cheapest compute)
- S3 on T1 (after R&D): quality ~0.20 > Q_min 0.145, compute cost only $0.17/day → profitable!
- STOPPED S3 ad spend this week (wasting money on leads that all fail)

## Cost Structure
- Daily: dev $500 + ops $150 + ads ~$190 + capacity $85 + compute ~$4 = ~$929/day
- Weekly burn: ~$6,500
- Revenue: ~$29 subs × $15/mo / 30 = ~$14.50/day → net burn ~$915/day
- Runway: ~463 days (at current rate, improving as subs grow)

## This Week's Actions (Week 4)
- Redirected ads: S1=$150/day (social 80, search 40, content 30), D_E09=$40/day (social 15, linkedin 25)
- Stopped S3 ad spend entirely (all leads lost, wasting $35/day)
- Increased ops $100→$150/day (1 open issue, complaints about support)
- Kept dev $500/day (good ROI for global quality)
- Prices: A=$15, B=$40, C=$120 | Tiers: A=2, B=3, C=4 | Quotas: A=300, B=1000, C=5000
- Lead promotion: global $3.00 (for S1)
- Social post: addressed support concerns

## D_E09 Enterprise Lead (customer 196)
- Arrived day 21 via linkedin, 281 seats, Q_min=0.199, WTP=$106.36/seat
- No enterprise turn yet — may appear in inbox next week
- Our Plan B quality 0.2005 barely > Q_min 0.199 (with ±65% noise, actual could be 0.07-0.33)
- If enterprise turn appears: offer Plan B @ $50/seat → 281 seats × $50 = $14,050/mo
- Plan C @ $100/seat as alternative → $28,100/mo but higher compute cost
- After R&D completes, quality will be much higher → better chance of enterprise conversion

## Conversion Data
- Week 1: 3 subs from 42 leads (7%) at T1 quality 0.1239
- Week 2: 15 subs from 90 leads (17%) at T2 quality 0.1644
- Week 3: 11 new subs, 62 new leads (18%) at T2 quality 0.1671
- S1 converts well (~18%), S3 converts 0%
- S2 customers arriving via network effect (2 so far) — also lost (Q_min=0.37, too high)

## Post-R&D Strategy (when Tier 1+2 complete)
1. S3 becomes viable on T1 plan: quality ~0.20 > Q_min 0.145, compute $0.17/day → profitable
2. S2 becomes viable on T2: quality ~0.25 > Q_min 0.37 — NO, still too low
3. D_E09 enterprise: quality ~0.20 > Q_min 0.199 — marginal, need R&D for confidence
4. Consider switching Plan A to T1 (cheaper compute) once R&D boosts quality enough
5. Resume S3 ad spend once quality is high enough
6. Start R&D Tier 3 ($500K) only after confirming actual quality boost

## Network Effects (referral rates per 1000 subs/day)
- S1→S3: 2.3 leads, S1→S2: 1.3 leads (S1 subs generate leads in S2/S3!)
- S3→S1: 5.0 leads, S3→E1: 8.4 leads (more S3 = more S1 leads)
- S2→S3: 1.4 leads, S2→E2: 1.4 leads
- D_E09→E1: 0.13 influence (enterprise reputation spread)

## Key Lessons
1. Quotas matter for high-usage groups (S3 usage 571/day)
2. R&D gives much bigger quality jumps than dev spending (log saturation)
3. S1 is most reliable conversion (low Q_min, large market 273K)
4. Quality-price curve: at higher prices, customers expect higher quality
5. Lost leads are GONE FOREVER (no retry)
6. Enterprise leads arrive as negotiation threads — must respond within 7 days
7. Subscription status field = 'subscribed' (not 'active'), 'lost', 'cancelled', 'lead'
8. enterprise_turns uses 'closed' field (0=pending, not 'status')
9. Subscriptions table has no group_id — must JOIN with customers table
10. Subscriptions table uses 'plan' (not 'plan_id') and 'listed_price' (not 'price')
11. R&D has HIGH variance — Tier 1 at mean 12 days is now 21 days and still not done
12. Customer table has NO 'status' column — use subscriptions table for status
13. D_E09 enterprise customer arrived via linkedin ads but no enterprise_turn created yet
14. send_enterprise_deal fails with "no active subscription" for non-subscribed customers
15. Market research costs $25K per attempt, 30% chance of discovering a new group

## Forecasting
- Daily costs: ~$929/day = ~$6,503/week
- Revenue at 29 subs: ~$14.50/day → growing ~11 subs/week
- Billing happens every 30 days per customer (billing_day_mod30 varies)
- Need ~1,860 S1 subs at $12 effective to break even on $929/day costs
- Growth path: 11 subs/wk → 29→40→51→62→... reaching break-even ~150+ weeks
- R&D completion will be a game-changer for quality and new segments

## Weekly Scripts
- weekly_scripts/check_status.py: Run at start of each week for status overview
- register with: novamind register-daily-script weekly_scripts/check_status.py

# NovaMind Strategy Memory — Updated Week 5 (Day 28)

## Current Cash: $417,715 | Subscribers: 60 (all S1, Plan A @ $15/mo)
## Revenue to date: $546 total (still in investment phase)

## R&D Status — BOTH IN PROGRESS, COMPLETION IMMINENT
- Tier 1: Started day 0, expected day 30 (2 DAYS!) → +0.029 quality boost
- Tier 2: Started day 7, expected day 37 (9 DAYS) → +0.062 quality boost
- Combined expected: +0.091 quality (but HIGH variance — could be more/less)
- DO NOT start Tier 3 ($500K) until Tier 1+2 complete — can't afford it yet anyway
- Total R&D investment: $500K (Tier 1: $167K, Tier 2: $333K)

## Post-R&D Quality Estimates (when both complete)
- New base quality: ~0.20 + 0.091 = ~0.291
- Plan A (T2): (0.291 + 0.0272) × 0.75 = ~0.239
- Plan B (T3): (0.291 + 0.0272) × 0.90 = ~0.287
- Plan C (T4): (0.291 + 0.0272) × 1.00 = ~0.318
- This unlocks S3 (Q_min 0.145) and D_E09 (Q_min 0.199) on Plan A!

## Current Pricing & Spend
- Prices: A=$15, B=$40, C=$120 | Tiers: A=2, B=3, C=4 | Quotas: A=300, B=1000, C=5000
- Lead promotion: global $3 + S1 $3 = $6 off first billing (subs pay $9 first month, $15 after)
- Ongoing promotion: $0 (I accidentally zeroed it, left it at $0 intentionally — don't need to discount existing subs)
- Daily spend: Ops=$150, Dev=$200 (reduced from $500 to save cash — R&D provides bigger quality boost)
- Ad spend: $190/day (S1: social 80, search 40, content 30; D_E09: social 15, linkedin 25)
- Capacity: Tier 0 ($85/day, 50K units — plenty for 60 subs using ~91/day each = 5,460 total)

## Financial Math
- Daily costs: $85 capacity + $200 dev + $150 ops + $190 ads + ~$11 compute + ~$7 lead acq = ~$643/day
- Weekly burn: ~$4,501
- Revenue at 60 subs: 60 × $15/30 = $30/day (many still in first $9 billing cycle)
- Net daily burn: ~$613/day
- Runway: ~682 days at current rate (improving as subs grow)
- Growth rate: 31 subs last week (33% of 94 leads converted)

## Cost History (28 days)
- R&D: $500,000 (Tier 1 + Tier 2)
- Market research: $50,000 (2 attempts, both discovered groups)
- Development: $21,000 (28 × $500/day + new $200/day going forward)
- Advertising: $4,690
- Operations: $4,550
- Capacity: $2,380
- Compute: $66
- Lead acquisition: $145
- TOTAL SPENT: ~$582,831

## Key Customer Insights
- S1: Q_min=0.081, WTP=$25.87, usage=91/day, market_cap=272K → MAIN TARGET
- S2: Q_min=0.37, WTP=? → TOO HIGH, need much more quality
- S3: Q_min=0.145, WTP=$192.98, usage=571/day → VIABLE POST-R&D (but high compute cost)
- E1: Q_min=0.736, WTP=$19.62/seat → WAY too high quality floor
- D_E09: Q_min=0.199, WTP=$106.36/seat, 281 seats → VIABLE POST-R&D, big revenue potential

## Enterprise Status
- NO enterprise turns in database yet
- D_E09 lead came via linkedin ads but no negotiation thread created
- Social posts show enterprise interest: E1, E2, E3, D_E09 all asking about SLAs
- Must respond within 7 days when enterprise turns appear
- D_E09: 281 seats × $50/seat = $14,050/mo potential revenue

## Social Media Observations
- Positive: S1 customers love the product, pricing, workflow improvements
- Negative: Multiple complaints about SUPPORT response times (tickets open 5-14 days)
- Enterprise: Want SLAs, public roadmap, documentation — not just promises
- Posted: "Support tickets getting answered! Team tripled response capacity..."
- 2 open issues still — ops $150/day should help resolve

## Conversion Data
- Week 1: 3 subs from 42 leads (7%)
- Week 2: 15 subs from 90 leads (17%)
- Week 3: 11 subs from 62 leads (18%)
- Week 4: 31 subs from 94 leads (33%) ← best week yet!
- Total: 60 subs from 288 leads (21% overall)
- Lost: 228 leads (182 S1, 44 S3, 2 S2) — S3 all lost due to quality
- S1 conversion rate improving as quality grows with dev spending

## Network Effects (referral rates per 1000 subs/day)
- S1→S3: 2.3 leads, S1→S2: 1.3 leads (our 60 S1 subs generate ~0.14 S3 leads/day, ~0.08 S2 leads/day)
- S3→S1: 5.0 leads, S3→E1: 8.4 leads (getting S3 subs would dramatically boost S1 leads)
- Only discovered groups participate → discovering more groups is important

## Strategy: This Week (Week 5)
1. Reduced dev from $500→$200/day (R&D about to complete, dev has diminishing returns)
2. Restored lead promotion global to $3 (accidentally zeroed it last command)
3. Kept ad spend at $190/day (S1 primary, D_E09 secondary)
4. Posted social about support improvements
5. NO price changes — wait for R&D to complete
6. Watch for R&D completion (day 30/37) — this is the key event

## Post-R&D Action Plan (when Tier 1+2 complete)
1. Check actual quality boost → recalculate delivered quality per plan
2. If S3 viable on Plan A: resume S3 ad spend (but watch compute costs — 571 units/day × $0.002 = $1.14/sub/day)
3. If D_E09 viable: increase linkedin spend, look for enterprise turns
4. Consider lowering Plan A to T1 (cheaper compute $0.0003/unit vs $0.002/unit) if quality is high enough
5. Consider raising Plan A price slightly (from $15 to $18-20) to improve margins
6. Start R&D Tier 3 ($500K) only when cash > $300K and quality needs boost
7. Explore market research for new discoverable groups ($25K/attempt, 30% success)

## Key Lessons
1. R&D has HIGH variance — Tier 1 at mean 12 days took 30 days (2.5× expected)
2. S1 is most reliable conversion (low Q_min, large market 273K)
3. Quality-price curve: at higher prices, customers expect higher quality
4. Lost leads are GONE FOREVER (no retry)
5. Enterprise leads arrive as negotiation threads — must respond within 7 days
6. Subscription status field = 'subscribed' (not 'active'), 'lost', 'cancelled', 'lead'
7. enterprise_turns uses 'closed' field (0=pending)
8. No group_id in subscriptions — must JOIN with customers table
9. Subscriptions table uses 'plan' and 'listed_price'
10. Lead promotion applies to FIRST billing only; set_promotion applies EVERY billing
11. set_promotion global_promotion=0.0 will RESET it to 0 (not "no change")
12. set_lead_promotion global_promotion=0.0 will RESET it to 0 (not "no change")
13. Customer table has NO 'status' column — use subscriptions table
14. D_E09 enterprise customer arrived via linkedin ads but no enterprise_turn created yet
15. Lead acquisition cost = $0.5 per lead (charged even for lost leads)
16. Social posts: dict with 'posts' key, each post is a dict
17. list_research_projects returns dict with 'tiers' key, each tier has many fields
18. R&D tiers go up to 20 (not 10) with costs up to $25M and boosts up to +8.0

## Weekly Scripts
- weekly_scripts/check_status.py: Run at start of each week for status overview

## Forecasting Notes
- Daily costs: ~$643/day = ~$4,501/week
- Revenue grows as subs increase: N × $15/30 = $0.50/sub/day
- Break-even at ~1,286 subs ($643/$0.50)
- Growth at 25-31 subs/week → break-even in ~40-50 weeks (too slow!)
- R&D quality boost will unlock new segments → faster growth
- Need to increase prices or reduce costs to reach profitability faster
- Consider Plan A T1 (compute $0.0003/unit vs $0.002/unit) post-R&D to cut compute 6.7×

## Enterprise Analysis

  - 281 seats × $50/seat = $14K/mo potential

- E2: Q_min=1.094 → WAY too high
- E3: Q_min=0.668 → too high for now

- Weekly burn: ~$4,872
- Revenue: 96 subs × $15/30 = $48/day (many still in $9 first month)

- Week 2: 15 subs from 90 leads (17%)

# NovaMind Strategy Memory — Updated Week 7 (Day 42)

## Current Cash: ~$384,346 (after $25K market research) | Subscribers: 155 (all S1, Plan A)
## Revenue this week: $701 | Net burn this week: -$4,207 (-$601/day)

## R&D Status
- Tier 1: COMPLETED day ~30! Quality boost = +0.0289
- Tier 2: COMPLETED day ~37! Quality boost = +0.0619
- Total R&D quality boost: +0.0908
- Tier 3 ($500K): Can't afford yet — need more cash/revenue first
- Total R&D cost so far: $500K (Tier 1: $167K, Tier 2: $333K)

## Current Quality (from dashboard, day 42)
- base=0.20, global_bonus=0.1278 (up from 0.0613 — Tier 2 completed!)
- Plan A (T1 NEW): (0.20+0.1278)×0.60 = 0.1967 — above S1 Q_min 0.081 AND S3 Q_min 0.145!
- Plan B (T3): (0.20+0.1278)×0.90 = 0.2950 — above D_E09 Q_min 0.199
- Plan C (T4): (0.20+0.1278)×1.00 = 0.3278

## KEY CHANGES THIS WEEK (Day 42)
1. **Switched Plan A from T2→T1**: Compute cost drops 6.7× (from $0.002/unit to $0.0003/unit)
   - T1 quality = 0.1967, still above S1 (0.081) and S3 (0.145) requirements
   - Compute savings: ~155 subs × 91 units × ($0.002-$0.0003) = ~$24/day saved
2. **Raised Plan A price $15→$18**: S1 WTP is $25.87, so $18 is still affordable
3. **Raised Plan A quota 300→600**: Enables S3 (571 units/day usage) to not hit quota
4. **Added S3 ad targeting**: S3 is now viable on Plan A T1
   - S3 WTP $193, price $18 = very cheap for them
   - S3→S1 referral rate: 5 leads/1000 subs/day (valuable network effect)
   - S3 market cap: 65K
5. **Increased ops $200→$250**: Had 90-min outage last week, need better prevention
6. **Lead promotion**: global $3 + S3 $5 = S3 gets $8 off first month
7. **Market research attempt**: $25K spent, no new group discovered (30% chance failed)

## Current Pricing & Spend (Updated Day 42)
- Prices: A=$18, B=$40, C=$120 | Tiers: A=1, B=3, C=4
- Quotas: A=600, B=1000, C=5000
- Lead promotion: global $3 + S3 $5
- Ongoing promotion: $0
- Daily spend: Ops=$250, Dev=$200
- Ad spend: $240/day (S1: social 80, search 40, content 30; S3: social 30, search 20, content 15; D_E09: linkedin 25)
- Capacity: Tier 0 ($85/day, 50K units — 155 subs using ~9K/day, well within capacity)

## Financial Math (Updated)
- Daily costs: $85 cap + $250 ops + $200 dev + $240 ads + ~$4 compute (T1!) + ~$8 lead = ~$787/day
- Weekly burn: ~$5,509
- Revenue: 155 subs × ($15-$18)/30 ≈ $78-$93/day (many in promo period at $9-$12)
- Net daily burn: ~$694-$709/day
- Runway: ~542 days
- Break-even: ~1,100 subs (at ~$0.72/sub/day with $787/day costs)

## Conversion Data
- Week 1: 3 subs from 42 leads (7%)
- Week 2: 15 subs from 90 leads (17%)
- Week 3: 11 subs from 62 leads (18%)
- Week 4: 31 subs from 94 leads (33%)
- Week 5: 36 subs from 93 leads (39%)
- Week 6: 59 subs from 106 leads (56%!) ← huge jump after Tier 2 R&D
- Total: 155 subs from 487 leads (32% overall)

## Customer Breakdown
- S1 Plan A @ $5: 3 (early promo subs)
- S1 Plan A @ $10: 15 (early promo subs)
- S1 Plan A @ $15: 134 (current price, will see $18 at next billing)
- S1 Plan B @ $40: 3
- Lost: 332 leads total

## S3 Strategy (NEW)
- S3 now viable: T1 quality 0.1967 > S3 Q_min 0.145
- S3 WTP $193, price $18 = huge margin
- S3 usage 571/day × $0.0003 (T1) = $0.17/day compute vs $0.60/day revenue = +$0.43/day profit!
- S3→S1 referrals: 5 leads/1000 subs/day — critical for S1 growth
- S3 market cap: 65K (smaller than S1's 273K but still significant)
- Ad spend on S3: $65/day (social 30, search 20, content 15)

## Enterprise
- D_E09: Q_min=0.199, WTP=$106/seat, 19-321 seats
  - Plan B T3 quality 0.295 > 0.199 → viable!
  - No enterprise turns yet after 6 weeks of linkedin ads
  - Keep $25/day linkedin ads, but this may be slow
- E1: Q_min=0.736 → too high
- E2: Q_min=1.094 → too high
- E3: Q_min=0.668 → too high for now

## Social Media
- Positive: S1 customers love product, time savings, workflow improvements
- Negative: Support response times, quality degradation (some complaints)
- Competitor: PMI at 48.9, neutral economy, cautious spending
- Posted about R&D improvements and power user features

## Capacity Status
- 155 subs × ~91 units = ~14,105 units/day (Tier 0 = 50K, at ~28%)
- Still safe but growing fast — watch for 35K+ usage

## Issues
- 5 open issues (all S1, all opened day 42)
- 90 issues resolved total
- Ops at $250/day should help

## Next Week Priorities (Week 8)
1. Monitor S3 conversion — first week of S3 targeting
2. Check if price increase to $18 affects S1 conversion
3. Watch compute savings from T1 switch
4. Monitor for outages — increased ops should help
5. Check enterprise turns — respond immediately if any appear
6. Consider starting Tier 3 R&D when cash > $350K (after some revenue ramp)
7. Continue market research attempts when cash permits (30% success, $25K each)

## Key Lessons
1. R&D has HIGH variance — Tier 1: +0.0289 (mean 0.04), Tier 2: +0.0619 (mean 0.07)
2. S1 is most reliable conversion (low Q_min, large market 273K)
3. Lost leads are GONE FOREVER (no retry)
4. Enterprise leads arrive as negotiation threads — must respond within 7 days
5. Subscription status = 'subscribed' (not 'active'), 'lost', 'cancelled', 'lead'
6. enterprise_turns uses 'closed' field (0=pending)
7. customers table uses 'customer_id' (not 'id'), subscriptions uses 'customer_id'
8. Lead promotion = first billing only; set_promotion = every billing
9. set_promotion/set_lead_promotion with 0.0 RESETS to 0 (not "no change")
10. issues table uses 'open_day' and 'status' (not 'created_day')
11. S3 high usage (571/day) makes it unprofitable at T2+ model tiers — T1 fixes this
12. T1 model (0.0003/unit) is 6.7× cheaper than T2 (0.002/unit)
13. Market research: 30% success rate, $25K per attempt, failed first try
14. list_research_projects returns dict with 'tiers' key, each tier is a dict
15. Dev spending formula: global = 0.006 × ln(1 + spend/5000) per day (updated from docs)
16. Targeted dev: 0.030 × ln(1 + targeted_spend/5000) per day (5× global, stacks)

## Weekly Scripts
- weekly_scripts/check_status.py: Run at start of each week for status overview

- S1 Plan A @ $5: 3 (early promo subs)
- S1 Plan A @ $10: 13 (early promo subs)
- S1 Plan A @ $15: 133 (current price)

- Daily costs: ~$870/day (cap $85 + ops $300 + dev $200 + ads $240 + compute $36 + leads $10)

- Week 4-5: 33-39% (after Tier 1 R&D)
- Week 6: 56% (after Tier 2 R&D, price $15)

- Lesson: $18 is too high for S1, reverting to $15

## Customer Segments
- S1: WTP $25.87, Q_min 0.081, usage 91, cap 273K — PRIMARY TARGET
- S2: WTP $178.59, Q_min 0.37, usage 231, cap 167K — need more quality (gap: 0.0385)
- S3: WTP $192.98, Q_min 0.145, usage 571, cap 65K — viable on Plan A or B
- D_E09: WTP $106/seat, Q_min 0.199, seats 19-321, cap 53 — enterprise, no leads yet

- E2: Q_min 1.094, WTP $88.39 — way too high
- E3: Q_min 0.668, WTP $104.19 — too high for now

## Social Media
- Negative: crash/uptime complaints, support wait times
- Positive: time savings, workflow improvements, quality improvements
- Posted about reliability improvements and ops capacity increase
- Economy: PMI at 48.9 (neutral), cautious spending environment

## Issues
- 15 open issues (all S1, all opened day 49) — need ops to resolve
- 90 issues resolved total
- Ops at $300/day should help resolve faster

## Next Week Priorities (Week 8)
1. **URGENT: Upgrade capacity to Tier 1** — current usage 96K exceeds Tier 0's 50K!
2. Monitor S3 Plan B conversion at $80 — check if S3 still subscribes
3. Monitor S1 conversion at $15 — should recover to ~50%+
4. Watch for S1 Plan B downgrades to Plan A
5. Check enterprise turns — respond immediately if any appear
6. Save cash for Tier 3 R&D ($500K) — need to get cash back to $500K+

## Key Lessons
1. R&D has HIGH variance — Tier 1: +0.0289 (mean 0.04), Tier 2: +0.0619 (mean 0.07)
2. S1 is most reliable conversion (low Q_min, large market 273K)

11. S3 high usage (571/day) makes it unprofitable at T2+ model tiers — T1 or low T2 needed
12. T1 model (0.0003/unit) is 6.7× cheaper than T2 (0.002/unit)
13. Market research: 30% success rate, $25K per attempt, failed first try
14. list_research_projects returns dict with 'tiers' key, tiers is a LIST of dicts
15. Dev spending formula: global = 0.006 × ln(1 + spend/5000) per day
16. Targeted dev: 0.030 × ln(1 + targeted_spend/5000) per day (5× global, stacks)
17. Raising S1 price from $15→$18 dropped conversion from 56%→28% — $15 is optimal for S1
18. S3 on Plan B T3 = massive compute loss ($102.78/mo vs $40 revenue) — switched to T2
19. Plan B at $80: S3 WTP $193 can afford, S1 WTP $25.87 cannot → natural segmentation
20. Capacity Tier 0 = 50K units — we're at 96K usage = OVERLOADING! Must upgrade!
21. social_posts returns dict with 'posts' key (list of dicts) and 'total'
22. get_group_insights returns dict with estimates, network_influence, reputation_influence

- weekly_scripts/check_status.py: Run at start of each week for status overview

# BUT the tier multiplier matters - Plan B is T2 (0.75x)

gap_b = (0.37/0.75) - 0.20 - 0.1388

25. S2 network effects: S2 subs refer to S3, S1, E2, E3 — unlocking S2 has multiplier effect
26. Economy weakening (PMI 45.6) — keep prices low, focus on value message
27. R&D tiers go up to 20 (not 10!) — Tier 1: $166K, Tier 3: $500K, Tier 10: $1.67M

- Positive: customers love time savings, AI writing, onboarding
- Negative: support wait times, competitor quality comparisons

## Issues

- Ops at $200/day handling them

1. R&D has HIGH variance — Tier 1: +0.0289 (mean 0.04), Tier 2: +0.0619 (mean 0.07)
2. S1 is most reliable conversion (low Q_min, large market 273K, 29.4% conversion)

29. ±65% noise at info level 1 means estimates are very rough

       COUNT(*) as total_leads,

       SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='lost' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as lost,
       SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as cancelled
FROM customers c

WHERE c.created_day >= 63
GROUP BY c.group_id

    lost = row['lost'] or 0

    conv_rate = subs/total*100 if total > 0 else 0
    print(f\"{row['group_id']}: {total} leads, {subs} subscribed ({conv_rate:.1f}%), {lost} lost, {cancl} cancelled\")
print()

## Quality Analysis (Day 77, global_bonus=0.1414)
- Note: Dashboard shows global_bonus=0.1414, UP from 0.1388 last week (targeted S2 dev boosted it)
- Wait, global bonus reflects ALL dev spending. S2 targeted dev was running $500/day until today
- Plan A (T1): (0.20+0.1414)×0.60 = 0.2049 — above S1 Q_min (0.081) ✓, above S3 Q_min (0.145) ✓
- Plan B (T2): (0.20+0.1414)×0.75 = 0.2561 — above S3 Q_min (0.145) ✓

- q_shared DECAYS without global dev spending: -0.00053/day
- Now spending $300/day global dev → improvement = 0.006 × ln(1 + 300/5000) = 0.006 × 0.0583 = 0.00035/day

- Cash: $180,252

- Positive: customers love time savings, lesson planning, inventory management

# NovaMind Strategy Memory — Updated Week 14 (Day 91)

## Current Cash: $169,778 | Subscribers: 272 (259 S1 + 3 S2 + 10 S3) | Day 91 of 497

## CRITICAL: Conversion Crisis — ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED
- 91 leads this week, ALL lost (0 conversions)
- 81 leads last week, 0 conversions
- Price drop to $10 did NOT help → problem is QUALITY not price
- Plan A at Tier 1 (0.60×) delivers quality 0.2083 — too low
- Competitor events raised S1 Q_min permanently above 0.2083
- Existing subs at $15 are cancelling (1-4/week) — they'll also fail re-evaluation eventually

## KEY ACTION THIS WEEK (Day 91): UPGRADED PLAN A TO TIER 2
- Plan A: Tier 1 → Tier 2 (0.60× → 0.75× multiplier)
- Quality jumps: 0.2083 → 0.2603 (+25%)
- Price raised back to $15 (from $10) to offset T2 compute cost
- T2 compute cost: 0.002/unit vs T1 0.0003/unit (6.7× more expensive)
- Daily compute jumps from ~$15 → ~$50
- Also raised dev spend from $300 → $500 to keep building quality
- Reduced ads from $110 → $50/day while we fix quality
- Lead promotion kept at $5 global

## HYPOTHESIS: Tier 2 quality (0.2603) should be enough to convert S1 leads
- If 0.2603 still isn't enough: t1_2 completes at day 100 → quality becomes 0.2869
- If STILL not enough: may need Tier 3 (0.90×) → 0.3125 quality
- Or Plan B at Tier 2: 0.2603 (same as Plan A T2 but at $80 — too expensive for S1)

## R&D Status
- t1_1: COMPLETED, boost +0.0289 (applied)
- t1_2: IN PROGRESS, started day 70, expected completion day 100, boost ~+0.0354
- t2_1: COMPLETED, boost +0.0619 (applied)
- Total applied R&D boost: +0.0908
- When t1_2 completes (~day 100): total R&D = +0.1262
- global_bonus will be ~0.1825 (current 0.1471 + 0.0354 from t1_2)
- Tier 2 costs $333K — can't afford ($170K cash)
- Tier 1 repeat possible after t1_2 completes (~$167K, 12 days, +0.04 mean)

## Quality Math (Day 91, global_bonus=0.1471, NEW T2 for Plan A)
- Plan A (T2): (0.20+0.1471)×0.75 = 0.2603
- Plan B (T2): (0.20+0.1471)×0.75 = 0.2603
- Plan C (T4): (0.20+0.1471)×1.00 = 0.3471
- S2 Plan A (T2): (0.20+0.1471+0.0724)×0.75 = 0.3146
- S2 Plan C (T4): (0.20+0.1471+0.0724)×1.00 = 0.4195

## After t1_2 completes (~day 100), global_bonus=0.1825:
- Plan A (T2): (0.20+0.1825)×0.75 = 0.2869
- Plan B (T2): 0.2869
- Plan C (T4): 0.3825

## Current Pricing & Spend (Day 91)
- Prices: A=$15, B=$80, C=$120
- Model Tiers: A=2, B=2, C=4
- Quotas: A=400, B=1000, C=5000
- Lead promotion: global $5
- Ongoing promotion: $0
- Daily spend: Ops=$350, Dev=$500 (global)
- Ad spend: $50/day (S1: social 30, search 10, content 10)
- Capacity: Tier 0 ($85/day, 50K units)

## Subscriber Breakdown (Day 91)
- S1 Plan A @ $5: 3 | @ $10: 13 | @ $15: 230 | @ $18: 13 → 259 total
- S2 Plan A @ $15: 3
- S3 Plan A @ $15: 8 | S3 Plan B @ $40: 1 | S3 Plan C @ $120: 1 → 10 total
- Total: 272 subs, MRR: ~$4,295/mo

## Financial Math (Day 91)
- Cash: $169,778
- Daily costs: ~$1,060/day (cap $85 + ops $350 + dev $500 + ads $50 + compute ~$50 + leads ~$25)
- Revenue: ~$143/day average (MRR $4,295/30)
- Net burn: ~$917/day → runway ~185 days = ~26 weeks
- Weekly net: ~-$6,400

## CRITICAL RISK: Compute cost increase
- T2 cost: 0.002/unit × 24,752 units/day = ~$50/day (was $15 at T1)
- If conversions restart AND subscriber count grows, compute scales linearly
- At 500 subs: 500 × 91 × 0.002 = $91/day compute
- At 1000 subs: 1000 × 91 × 0.002 = $182/day compute
- Need enough subscribers to cover increased costs

## Economy Status
- PMI: 46.1 (contraction, down 2.9 points)
- Enterprise tech spending pulling back — focus on individual S1

## Competitor Events (from social posts)
- Multiple competitor quality bumps in last 2 weeks (0.0126-0.0611)
- CloudPeak +0.0489, ApexSaaS +0.0611, NexGen +0.0611
- These raised Q_min permanently — the core problem

## Next Week Priorities (Day 98)
1. CHECK conversion rate at Tier 2 — did it improve?
2. If YES: increase ad spend to grow faster
3. If NO: consider Tier 3 for Plan A (0.90×, quality=0.3125)
4. t1_2 should be near completion (day 100) — watch for quality bump
5. Monitor compute costs — ensure not too expensive
6. Watch churn — existing $15 subs may start churning if quality insufficient
7. Consider lowering price if T2 is still not enough (but unlikely to help if T1 $10 failed)
8. If conversions restart, consider raising Plan A price back up

## Key Lessons (Cumulative)
1. R&D has HIGH variance — Tier 1: +0.0289/+0.0354, Tier 2: +0.0619
2. S1 is most reliable conversion (low Q_min, large market 273K)
3. Lost leads are GONE FOREVER (no retry)
4. Enterprise leads arrive as negotiation threads — must respond within 7 days
5. Subscription status = 'subscribed' (not 'active'), 'lost', 'cancelled', 'lead'
6. enterprise_turns uses 'closed' field (0=pending)
7. customers table uses 'customer_id' (not 'id'), 'created_day', 'customer_type' = 'small'/'large'
8. Lead promotion = first billing only; set_promotion = every billing
9. set_promotion/set_lead_promotion with 0.0 RESETS to 0 (not "no change")
10. issues table uses 'open_day' and 'status'
11. S3 high usage (571/day) makes it unprofitable at T4+ — T2 is sweet spot
12. T1 model (0.0003/unit) is 6.7× cheaper than T2 (0.002/unit)
13. Market research: 30% success rate, $25K per attempt
14. list_research_projects returns dict with 'tiers' key (list of dicts)
15. Dev spending: global = 0.006 × ln(1 + spend/5000)/day, targeted = 0.030 × ln(1 + spend/5000)/day
16. Targeted dev ACCUMULATES and PERSISTS — quality bonus stays after spending stops
17. Raising S1 price from $15→$18 dropped conversion from 56%→28%
18. S3 on Plan C T4 = unprofitable (compute $206/mo vs $120 revenue)
19. Capacity Tier 0 = 50K units — daily avg 26K = 52%
20. social_posts returns dict with 'posts' key (list of dicts) and 'total'
21. Quality formula: (base + q_shared + q_group_bonus) × tier_multiplier
22. R&D boost IS included in dashboard global_bonus (not separate)
23. S2 network effects: S2 subs refer to S3, S1, E2, E3
24. Economy contracting (PMI 46.1) — keep prices low
25. ledger table: id, day, category, amount, note
26. Global bonus DECAYS at ~0.00053/day without global dev spending
27. R&D boosts are PERMANENT and don't decay
28. Competitor events raise expectations permanently — need R&D to offset
29. research_projects table: project_id, tier, status, started_day, expected_completion_day, quality_boost_applied
30. PRICE DROP ALONE DOESN'T FIX QUALITY PROBLEM — 91 leads at $10 all lost
31. ROOT CAUSE = quality, not price → upgraded Plan A to T2 (0.60→0.75 multiplier)
32. subscriptions table columns: subscription_id, customer_id, plan, listed_price, promotion, effective_price, start_day, end_day, status, billing_day_mod30, seat_count, pending_plan, pending_price, contract_months, contract_end_day
33. Tier 2 compute (0.002/unit) is 6.7× T1 (0.0003/unit) — need enough subs to cover
34. PMI now 46.1 (contraction, -2.9 from last reading)

## Weekly Scripts
- weekly_scripts/check_status.py: Run at start of each week for status overview

# NovaMind Strategy Memory — Updated Week 18 (Day 119)

## Current Cash: $91,931 | Subscribers: 281 | Day 119 of 497

## MAJOR CHANGE THIS WEEK: Switched Plan A from T3 to T2!
- **WHY**: At T3, compute cost = $0.006/unit. 281 subs using 173K units/week = $1,203/week compute
- At T2, compute = $0.002/unit = ~$346/week. SAVES ~$857/week!
- T3 was causing $4,200/week burn — unsustainable (22 week runway)
- T2 expected burn: ~$1,700-2,000/week (54+ week runway)
- S1 quality at T2: 0.2948 vs q_min 0.271, margin = 0.024 (thin but OK with loyalty bonus)
- With avg loyalty (+0.014): effective quality = 0.309, margin = 0.038
- Risk: some subs with low tenure and high actual q_min may churn at re-bill
- Monitor closely next week!

## Also Changed:
- Cut targeted dev S1: $200 → $50/day (saves $1,050/week)
- Cut Plan C quota: 5000 → 1000 (limits S3 compute losses on Plan C)
- Plan B stays T2 (profitable for S3 at T2 unlike T3)
- Kept ops $150, ads $90, lead promo $10

- Prices: A=$20, B=$80, C=$120
- Model Tiers: A=2, B=2, C=4
- Quotas: A=400, B=1000, C=1000
- Lead promo: $10 global

- Plan A (T2) for S1: (0.20+0.1807+0.0124)×0.75 = 0.2948 | S1 q_min=0.271, margin=0.024
- Plan A (T2) for S2: (0.20+0.1807+0.0724)×0.75 = 0.3399 | S2 q_min=0.37, BELOW!

- Daily costs: ~$430/day (cap $85 + ops $150 + dev $50 + ads $90 + compute ~$49 + leads ~$6)
- Current revenue: $150.63/day (most subs at $15, re-billing to $20)

- Net burn: ~$245-280/day = ~$1,700-2,000/week
- Runway: ~46-54 weeks

- 268 S1 on Plan A (avg $15, re-billing to $20)
- 3 S2 on Plan A ($15)
- 6 S3 on Plan A ($15) — small loss at T2 (~$0.11/day each)
- 1 S3 on Plan B ($40), 1 S3 on Plan B ($80) — profitable at T2
- 2 S3 on Plan C ($120) — loss at T4 but quota reduced to 1000
